00002| 
00003| :class:`History` subscribes to the :class:`~taskflow.events.EventBus` and folds
00004| the event stream into queryable structures. It never inspects the scheduler's
00005| internal state directly -- everything it knows, it learned from an event -- so
00006| it doubles as a check that the scheduler narrates its work faithfully.
00007| 
00008| The queries it answers:
00009| 
00010| * :meth:`History.run_order` -- the order in which jobs first started running.
00011| * :meth:`History.attempts_for` -- how many times a given job started (i.e. how
00012|   many attempts it made, counting retries).
00013| * :meth:`History.state_timeline` -- the ``(virtual_time, state)`` sequence a
00014|   job passed through.
00015| * :meth:`History.succeeded_jobs` / :meth:`History.failed_jobs` /
00016|   :meth:`History.skipped_jobs` -- the terminal outcome sets.
00017| * :meth:`History.peak_resource_usage` -- the high-water mark of a resource pool.
00018| 
00019| Topics consumed
00020| ---------------
00021| ``job.started``
00022|     Exact subscription. Feeds run order, attempt counts and per-job start log.
00023| ``job.state``
00024|     Exact subscription. Feeds the per-job state timeline.
00025| ``job.term`` (prefix)
00026|     Prefix subscription covering ``job.term.succeeded`` / ``job.term.failed`` /
00027|     ``job.term.skipped``. Feeds the terminal-outcome sets.
00028| ``resource.acquired`` / ``resource.released``
00029|     Exact subscriptions. Feed the running resource tally and its peak.
00030| """
00031| 
00032| from __future__ import annotations
00033| 
00034| from taskflow.model import State
00035| 
00036| 
00037| class History:
00038|     """Fold a scheduler's event stream into queryable run history.
00039| 
00040|     Construct with an :class:`~taskflow.events.EventBus` and the history wires
00041|     up all of its subscriptions immediately, so it captures every event
00042|     published from that point on.
00043|     """
00044| 
00045|     def __init__(self, bus):
00046|         self._bus = bus
00047| 
00048|         self._start_order = []          # ids in first-start order
00049|         self._start_seen = set()
00050|         self._attempts = {}             # id -> number of starts
00051|         self._timeline = {}             # id -> list of (at, State)
00052| 
00053|         self._succeeded = []            # ids, in the order they succeeded
00054|         self._failed = []
00055|         self._skipped = []
00056| 
00057|         self._usage = {}                # pool -> current units held
00058|         self._peak = {}                 # pool -> peak units held
00059|         self._events = []               # every event, for debugging/queries
00060| 
00061|         self._subscribe()
00062| 
00063|     # -- wiring -----------------------------------------------------------
00064| 
00065|     def _subscribe(self):
00066|         self._bus.subscribe("job.started", self._on_started)
00067|         self._bus.subscribe("job.state", self._on_state)
00068|         self._bus.subscribe_prefix("job.term", self._on_terminal)
00069|         self._bus.subscribe("resource.acquired", self._on_acquired)
00070|         self._bus.subscribe("resource.released", self._on_released)
00071| 
00072|     # -- handlers ---------------------------------------------------------
00073| 
00074|     def _on_started(self, event):
00075|         self._events.append(event)
00076|         task_id = event.get("id")
00077|         self._attempts[task_id] = self._attempts.get(task_id, 0) + 1
00078|         if task_id not in self._start_seen:
00079|             self._start_seen.add(task_id)
00080|             self._start_order.append(task_id)
00081| 
00082|     def _on_state(self, event):
00083|         self._events.append(event)
00084|         task_id = event.get("id")
00085|         state = event.get("state")
00086|         self._timeline.setdefault(task_id, []).append((event.at, state))
00087| 
00088|     def _on_terminal(self, event):
00089|         self._events.append(event)
00090|         task_id = event.get("id")
00091|         suffix = event.topic.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
00092|         if suffix == "succeeded":
00093|             self._succeeded.append(task_id)
00094|         elif suffix == "failed":
00095|             self._failed.append(task_id)
00096|         elif suffix == "skipped":
00097|             self._skipped.append(task_id)
00098| 
00099|     def _on_acquired(self, event):
00100|         self._events.append(event)
00101|         pool = event.get("pool")
00102|         cost = event.get("cost", 0)
00103|         self._usage[pool] = self._usage.get(pool, 0) + cost
00104|         if self._usage[pool] > self._peak.get(pool, 0):
00105|             self._peak[pool] = self._usage[pool]
00106| 
00107|     def _on_released(self, event):
00108|         self._events.append(event)
00109|         pool = event.get("pool")
00110|         cost = event.get("cost", 0)
00111|         self._usage[pool] = self._usage.get(pool, 0) - cost
00112| 
00113|     # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
00114| 
00115|     def run_order(self):
00116|         """Return the ids of jobs in the order they first started running."""
00117| 
00118|         return list(self._start_order)
00119| 
00120|     def attempts_for(self, task_id):
00121|         """Return how many times ``task_id`` started (attempts, incl. retries)."""
00122| 
00123|         return self._attempts.get(task_id, 0)
00124| 
00125|     def state_timeline(self, task_id):
00126|         """Return the ``(virtual_time, State)`` entries recorded for ``task_id``."""
00127| 
00128|         return list(self._timeline.get(task_id, []))
00129| 
00130|     def final_state(self, task_id):
00131|         """Return the last state recorded for ``task_id``, or ``None`` if unseen."""
00132| 
00133|         entries = self._timeline.get(task_id)
00134|         return entries[-1][1] if entries else None
00135| 
00136|     def succeeded_jobs(self):
00137|         """Return the ids that reached ``SUCCEEDED``, in completion order."""
00138| 
00139|         return list(self._succeeded)
00140| 
00141|     def failed_jobs(self):
00142|         """Return the ids that reached ``FAILED``, in completion order."""
00143| 
00144|         return list(self._failed)
00145| 
00146|     def skipped_jobs(self):
00147|         """Return the ids that were ``SKIPPED``, in the order they were skipped."""
00148| 
00149|         return list(self._skipped)
00150| 
00151|     def peak_resource_usage(self, pool):
00152|         """Return the high-water mark of concurrent units held in ``pool``."""
00153| 
00154|         return self._peak.get(pool, 0)
00155| 
00156|     def current_resource_usage(self, pool):
00157|         """Return the units currently held in ``pool`` (0 once a run is done)."""
00158| 
00159|         return self._usage.get(pool, 0)
00160| 
00161|     def events(self):
00162|         """Return every event the history observed, in delivery order."""
00163| 
00164|         return list(self._events)
00165| 
00166|     def events_on(self, topic):
00167|         """Return every observed event whose topic exactly equals ``topic``."""
00168| 
00169|         return [event for event in self._events if event.topic == topic]
00170| 
00171|     def total_attempts(self):
00172|         """Return the total number of attempts across every job (incl. retries)."""
00173| 
00174|         return sum(self._attempts.values())
00175| 
00176|     def retried_jobs(self):
00177|         """Return the ids of jobs that started more than once (were retried)."""
00178| 
00179|         return [tid for tid, n in self._attempts.items() if n > 1]
00180| 
00181|     def outcome_counts(self):
00182|         """Return a ``{outcome: count}`` tally of terminal outcomes.
00183| 
00184|         The keys are ``"succeeded"``, ``"failed"`` and ``"skipped"``; the values
00185|         are how many jobs reached each. Handy for a one-glance run summary.
00186|         """
00187| 
00188|         return {
00189|             "succeeded": len(self._succeeded),
00190|             "failed": len(self._failed),
00191|             "skipped": len(self._skipped),

00205|         Returns the most recent state recorded at or before ``when``, or
00206|         ``None`` if the job had not yet been seen by then.
00207|         """

00209|         result = None
00210|         for at, seen in self._timeline.get(task_id, []):

"""An event-sourced record of what happened during a scheduler run.

:class:`History` subscribes to the :class:`~taskflow.events.EventBus` and folds
the event stream into queryable structures. It never inspects the scheduler's
internal state directly -- everything it knows, it learned from an event -- so
it doubles as a check that the scheduler narrates its work faithfully.

The queries it answers:

* :meth:`History.run_order` -- the order in which jobs first started running.
* :meth:`History.attempts_for` -- how many times a given job started (i.e. how
  many attempts it made, counting retries).
* :meth:`History.state_timeline` -- the ``(virtual_time, state)`` sequence a
  job passed through.
* :meth:`History.succeeded_jobs` / :meth:`History.failed_jobs` /
  :meth:`History.skipped_jobs` -- the terminal outcome sets.
* :meth:`History.peak_resource_usage` -- the high-water mark of a resource pool.
